children: TXO Partners, L.P. reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $55.1 million, down 45% year over year, and a net loss of $32.1 million, compared with net income of $4.4 million a year earlier. The decline in revenue was driven mainly by a $68.3 million adverse year-over-year swing in derivative results.
Revenue was $55.1M, compared with $100.9M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change (45%).
Net loss was $32.1M, compared with net income of $4.4M in the prior-year quarter.
Diluted EPS was $(0.58), compared with $0.08 in the prior-year quarter.
Nine-month revenue declined 15% to $234.2 million as hedge losses and weaker natural gas prices outweighed higher oil and NGL prices.
Nine-month production increased 7% to 7.8 million Boe, supported by Williston Basin acquisitions and new wells, partly offset by asset sales and natural decline.
Cross Timbers property sales generated $101.3 million in proceeds. TXO began winding down the business in July 2026.
Drilling, completion and facilities spending totaled $79.2 million for the first nine months. Full-year 2026 spending is projected at $90 million to $95 million.
Management expects to fund development and distributions from operating cash flow and available liquidity, while retaining flexibility to adjust spending.
